scope: Source application framebuffer render and display-only power-control staging. No GPU tuning or registry write is part of the capture sequence. Actual source and subsequent packaged proof are distinct.
capture_method: Installed DearPyGUI output_frame_buffer, invoked after ordinary initial rendering. The Windows.Graphics.Capture COM failure is bypassed, not repaired.
source_visual_review: The original 450 W endpoint remains normal-colored.
The displayed 455 W value above the original bound is amber; the added slider segment has an amber tint.
The 350 W in-range staged case uses normal text within an extended displayed range.
Power widgets and original clock text restore after the sequence; normal refresh resumes.
hardware_check: Independent configured-state and complete rail-request readbacks are compared separately. Capture timestamps are bookkeeping, not GPU configuration.
packaged_verification_required: Match the final source-manifest hashes and compiled capture integration with the development EXE.
Run the actual packaged capture and inspect the produced PNGs, not only the source run.
Verify original configured GPU requests, full rail packets, image, registry and receipt state after capture.
remaining: Live REL and OV/ALT/VMIN panel rendering.
Remaining preview/error, Apply/Undo and recovery-dialog walkthrough.
Other DPI, viewport sizes and adapters.
qualification: Staged widget values are synthetic display cases. They do not establish an extended GPU request, power draw, firmware enforcement or a physical safety bound.

source_hardware_readback.normalization: Only the host-side diagnostic driver_flags.captured_at timestamp is omitted from its configuration comparison.
